jobs.title: Summer Camp Counselor with Leadership Advancement at Camp Augusta
jobs.description: Employer: Camp Augusta Expires: 11/26/2026 Camp Counselor- Leadership Track Opportunity Location: Northern California, United States (On-site housing provided)Position Type: Full-time, seasonal (May 18th-August 14th)Compensation: From $4500 + housing, utilities, organic meals, and professional mobility Make a Difference and Grow Your Skills for the FutureAre you passionate about youth development and looking for an impactful summer that doubles as a launchpad for your career? Camp Augusta offers a transformative experience where counselors are guides, mentors, and leaders who make a lasting difference in campers' lives; this role integrates especially well with those looking to grow professionally on a path in youth development, education, therapy, social work, or leadership roles. Beyond just a summer job, we invest deeply in your growth and offer individual training in the summer with the intention that you'd return the following summer in a leadership role. Why Choose Camp Augusta?Camp Augusta isn’t your average summer camp—here’s what makes us different:Unmatched Training: Begin with over 300 hours of in-depth training covering child development, emotional intelligence, and group dynamics. You’ll gain real tools for working with youth and teams in any future career.Structured Leadership Path: Counselors who shine have the opportunity to move up through various leadership roles in areas like program management, logistics, and staff support in future summers.Dynamic Programming: With 150+ activities (from archery to circus arts), no two days are alike. You’ll lead, teach, and innovate, all while building versatile skills.Human-Centered Approach: Grounded in Rational-Emotive Behavior Therapy and Nonviolent Communication, our program empowers campers and staff alike to grow through empathy, self-expression, and resilience. Your Role as a Camp Counselor (This Summer)As a Camp Counselor, you’ll be responsible for a cabin of 5 campers at a time, creating a safe, fun, and empowering environment that allows them to explore, grow, and make lasting memories. After completing our comprehensive training program, you’ll put your skills to use each day, leading activities, guiding campers, and contributing to the overall camp magic.Your Day at Camp Augusta will look like this:Creating Special Wake-Ups: Create a memorable and intentional Special Wake-Up for your cabin, setting the tone for a fun and meaningful day.Facilitating a Robust Variety of Clinics: Lead four different activity blocks each day from the wide array of activities you’ll choose to focus on during training. From circus arts to archery to crafts—your day is varied, creative, and full of new learning.Designing Cabin Activities: Lead your cabin in daily activities that promote teamwork, creativity, and self-expression, such as art projects, skits, or nature walks.Evening Programs: Be part of our evening programs, where you’ll play in large-scale games like capture the flag, or take on roles in immersive, creative camp-wide events. You’ll help make these programs unforgettable for campers through skits, songs, and your best character performances.Evening Embers: End each day with thoughtful, silly, and memorable activities (Embers) to help campers connect, reflect, and prepare for the days ahead.Give back with heart: Gift your campers two personal gifts each session: a hand-crafted wood cookie and a heartfelt Parent Letter, showing your investment in their growth and journey.Counselors are the heartbeat of camp, and our words are critical to bringing our hearts to theirs. Most counselors spend a session or two outside of the cabin as well, contributing to programming or other areas of interest. See our page on counselor life for more information on the role and how it differs from most other camps. Leadership Development - The Augusta Growth Track (This Summer and Beyond!)At Camp Augusta, we believe in investing in our counselors not just for the summer, but for the future. Our structured Leadership Track allows high-performing counselors to gain hands-on experience in program management, staff support, and logistics, preparing you for future roles within and beyond the camp. This generally looks like spending 3 weeks of the summer our of the cabin with an emphasis in participating and training in another domain.Leadership tracks offer in-summer training for the roles of:Master of Fun & Games: Have a flair for our epic games and activities? Work on logistics, staging, and game oversight, collaborating with our MFG team to run unforgettable camp programs.Village Leadership: Ready for a ‘cabin’ of young adults for a summer? Support fellow counselors alongside our Village Leaders, gaining experience in team management, parent communication, and more.Area Program Directors: Take the lead in domains with our Arts Directors, Challenge Course Managers, Equestrian Team, or Masters of Fun and Games.Office & Administration: Passionate about keeping camp running? Explore camp logistics behind the scenes, with roles in scheduling, holistic management, and programming coordination.More Specialized Areas!: Check out all of our non-counseling roles and identify the one you're most interested in. If your strengths match the role, we'll get you involved and trained.These experiences provide invaluable skills for careers in youth development, social work, education, counseling, and beyond. Who We’re Looking For:We seek energetic, passionate individuals eager to work with kids and committed to personal growth. You don’t need all the answers from day one; we’re here to mentor and support you.Minimum Requirements:Must be 19 or older by June 1st, 2027.Available for full summer: May 18th to August 14th, 2026 (includes 3.5 weeks of training and 9 weeks of summer camp).Ability to commit to ~5 hours/week of pre-camp onboarding fro the date you're hired till you arrive (depending on hire date)A strong desire to grow into a leadership position, with a commitment to returning for subsequent summers.AND MUST have two of the following: At least one summer of experience at a summer campOver 100 hours of direct professional (paid) mentorship work with youthA major or background directly related to working with youth, with the intention to work with youth in your future career Preferred Qualifications:Experience working with children in a meaningful way (e.g., previous camp, childcare, or mentorship experience)A passion for personal development and the ability to apply your learning to your work with campers. What You'll Receive:Competitive Compensation: $4500 for the summerFull Housing & Meals: Enjoy our on-site lodging and healthy, organic mealsComprehensive Training: Gain 300+ hours of training plus ongoing mentorship and leadership developmentAn Inspiring Community: Join a team of dedicated individuals who are as passionate about growth and impact as you are Internships?Yup, we do that. We can co-design your internship based on the skills and development you seek, and the specific requirements of your school!Note: Some educational institutions require prior approval before the start of an internship. It is the responsibility of the student to check with their institution to be sure they meet any requirements before they accept a position.If you have internship requirements, we can almost definitely meet them! About Camp Augusta:Camp Augusta is a nonprofit residential summer camp in northern California that offers a truly unique summer camp experience for campers and staff alike. We are focused on counseling skills, creativity, excellent programming, and camper choice - see more about the vision of our camp here.We aim to include and celebrate many facets of human identity – gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, race, age, neurodiversity, disability status, citizenship, and other aspects that make us unique. We are working to craft an inclusive culture founded on ideals of curiosity, honesty, empathy, and acceptance – a place where people are seen and acknowledged for their shared humanity as well as their unique individuality. Read our full Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, And Belonging (DEIB) Statement here. Do you have any questions?Send us a message on Handshake, and we'll get back to you by the end of the next day! You can also send any questions you have to applications@campaugusta.org.Feeling ready to apply?1. Take 5 minutes to fill out our interest form. 2. Someone from our hiring team will reach out to you within 24 hours.3. Schedule an Intro Chat with us, and complete a full application!

jobs.title: Fellows Program at Collegiate School
jobs.description: Employer: Collegiate School Expires: 11/27/2026 The Collegiate School Fellows’ Program is a one- to two-year teaching fellowship that is designed for early-career teachers and career-switchers who plan to pursue a career in education. We welcome applicants interested in teaching any grade level from JK-12 and in coaching Grades 7-12. Qualified candidates must demonstrate a sustained interest in children; possess college- or graduate-level coursework in their subject area and a track record of academic excellence; and have demonstrable experience in co-curricular areas such as sports and clubs.The purpose of the Fellows’ Program is to provide aspiring educators with the mentorship, classroom experience, and pedagogical background necessary to become a lead classroom teacher. In keeping with three of the School’s core values–love of learning, excellence, and community–the Program strives to foster and support each fellow’s lifelong journey in the field of education.Program Details:The program offers a thorough introduction to a career in education. Fellows receive personalized mentorship, preparation in pedagogy and instructional design, cultural competency training, extensive professional development, and job placement assistance. Upon completion of the fellowship, each fellow will possess the skills necessary to be a lead teacher or qualified candidate in their division or department.Each year, we hire a small cohort of fellows. Each fellow shares a classroom with a mentor teacher in their department or grade level. All fellows have regular meetings with their mentor, their department- or grade-level chair, the Fellows’ Program Director, the cohort of fellows, and the Dean of Faculty. Fellows also contribute to or participate in School activities such as advisory meetings, clubs, sports, and performances, and they attend relevant School events such as faculty meetings, assemblies, and professional development days. Fellows engage fully in the life of the School, thereby gaining experience with a school setting and insight into all aspects of a career in education, and they follow the same daily schedule as any classroom teacher in their divisionFellows receive a full-time salary and are eligible for benefits that include health, dental, and vision insurance; life insurance; free daily lunch; classroom supplies and teaching materials; all required texts; professional development support for on-and off-campus opportunities; and additional stipends for coaching and certain extracurricular activities. The program begins in mid-August with a week of new teacher training and another week of meetings for all faculty members, and it ends in early June at the conclusion of the school year.By the conclusion of the fellowship, participants will have created a professional dossier of job application materials, a body of work for lesson plans, and a career development plan. We are accepting applications through January 8, 2027. We will not be reviewing any applications until that time and wanted to make you aware of our timeline. It is critical that candidates demonstrate a commitment to the School’s Core Values and MissionHONORPersonal integrity and devotion to the truth, which make one trustworthy, forthright, responsible and fair.LOVE OF LEARNINGA creative spirit that promotes intellectual and personal growth through exploration, inquiry and openness to change.EXCELLENCE A sustained commitment to meeting high standards of character, achievement and personal accountability.RESPECTFundamental regard for the dignity and worth of each individual.COMMUNITYA commitment to responsive and compassionate citizenship and service on campus, in the local community and in the broader world.Required Competencies:Excellent communication skills with the ability to communicate the School’s shared purpose; builds trust among colleagues; is accountable; lives up to commitments.Proven cross cultural competency skills demonstrating self awareness, awareness of others and the ability to adopt inclusive perspectives, attitudes and behaviors to drive inclusion and belonging in the ongoing development and maintenance of an inclusive campus community.Demonstrates a strong commitment to a servant leadership model focusing on the growth and development of the team to successfully fulfill shared goals.Understands the big picture and handles areas of responsibility in a manner consistent with the School’s mission and values. Offers assistance within the office especially during busy times.Relates to the Collegiate community including faculty, staff, students, parents and applicants in a cooperative manner.Meets deadlines, demonstrates effective use of time and handles multiple assignments simultaneously.Understands the need for growth and is receptive to constructive feedback.Maintains confidentiality at all times.Who we areCollegiate School is a co-educational, independent day school located in Henrico County, within 20 minutes of downtown Richmond, Virginia, for students in Junior Kindergarten through 12th grade. For more than 100 years, Collegiate has nurtured inquisitive thinkers, responsible citizens, and compassionate leaders. Grounded in the values that have sustained it over the course of more than a century, Collegiate provides its nearly 1,700 students with an engaging academic environment dedicated to preparing them for a globally connected and changing world.The essence of Collegiate School is the richness of relationships among students, faculty, parents, administrators, and alumni in a dynamic learning community with high personal and academic expectations. This exceptional educational environment enables students to develop their potential for intellectual growth, leadership, and service.Why Collegiate? Collegiate School is well-regarded for developing students into citizens who lead, serve and shape the world. We do so with the help of a caring faculty and staff who also have opportunities to lead, serve and shape the world, through the young lives they touch.Below are just a few examples of some of the great advantages of working at Collegiate:Excellent professional development opportunities for faculty and staffCollaborative working environmentA rich employee benefits package (which includes free lunch!)Opportunities for growth and leadershipAn environment that fosters creative and innovative instruction

jobs.title: Emergency Mental Health Clinician (LMSW, LLMSW, LPC, LLP) at Integrated Services of Kalamazoo
jobs.description: Employer: Integrated Services of Kalamazoo Expires: 11/27/2026 Emergency Mental Health Clinician (LMSW, LLMSW, LPC, LLP)Starting Salary: $66,185 /yr, commensurate with experience – plus shift differential payFull Time, Second ShiftTwo Schedule Options Available: Four 10-hour days (12p – 10p), OR Five 8-hour days (12p – 8p)Do you have a passion for empowering individuals receiving behavioral health services toimprove their overall quality of life? Would you like to be a valuable member of a diversitydriven, mission-minded team that impacts our community? If so, we have an excitingopportunity for you to work as a full-time (40 hrs/wk) Emergency Mental Health Clinician!What You Will Be DoingIn this exhilarating position, you will be at the forefront of mental health support, working in the office, in the community, and in hospital settings. You’ll have the opportunity to provide crucial assistance to individuals in crisis, conduct thorough assessments, and connect them with ongoing services that can truly transform their lives. Join a dynamic team where you'll expand your clinical expertise through cross-training across our Emergency Mental Health and Access services, including Intensive Crisis Stabilization (ICS), Emergency Mental Health (EMH), and Mobile Crisis Response (MCR), while gaining experience with diverse patient populations and clinical settings.As an Emergency Mental Health Clinician, you will collaborate with a dedicated team, engaging in a role that makes a real difference in the Kalamazoo County community. Preferred scheduling options can be discussed during the interview process.What We RequireYou must have a Master’s Degree in Social Work, Psychology or a related field. Those with limited licensure are encouraged to apply – ISK provides professional license supervision for those with limited licensure.You’ll have extensive knowledge of the DSM-5 diagnostic criteria, co-occurring disorders,substance use disorders, evidence-based and promising practice interventions, and familiarity with psychotropic medications and the ability to work in a fast- paced environment. You must also have a valid Michigan Driver’s license and reliable transportation.Why Work For ISKBecause we make a difference in the lives of the individuals we serve in the Kalamazoo community every day. You will have the opportunity to work with amazing co-workers in an environment that values diversity, inclusion, work/life balance and encourages ongoing education for professional development.We also offer a competitive compensation and benefits package, with some of the best retirement plans in southwest Michigan including a 6.2% retirement match and pension plan!You will also enjoy 12 paid holidays, Generous PTO and the opportunity to earn additional PTO hours for participating in our wellness program! ISK works with youth, families, and adults with mental illnesses, intellectual and developmental disabilities, and substance use disorders to help them succeed. We provide welcoming and diverse community partnerships which collaborate and share resources to support individuals and families to be successful and achieve their goals in a trauma-informed environment.Come Join Us!Individuals of diverse racial, ethnic, and cultural backgrounds along with bilingual candidatesare invited to apply. ISK is an equal opportunity employer that encourages diversity andinclusion among its workforce. ISK fomenta la diversidad y la inclusión.We look forward to meeting you! Requires coordination of hands and/or eye/hand/foot and ability to hear and communicate verbally.Working Conditions – In office environment with noise from computers, copy machine, andtelephones. May encounter communityenvironments that include homes, schools, courts, and other community settings that may or may not be barrier-free. Travel throughout the Kalamazoo area may be required.

jobs.description: Employer: Ventura County Community College District Expires: 11/27/2026 Instructor In Culinary Arts/Food Technology (Part-Time Pool)Ventura County Community College District Salary:Job Type: Part-Time FacultyJob Number: 2026-00327Location: Oxnard College (Oxnard CA), CADepartment: OC - Academic AffairsClosing: ContinuousDescriptionWe are accepting applications on an on-going basis for future consideration for part-time instructors in this discipline at Oxnard College. Applications submitted to this pool will be kept on file for the Fall 2026, Spring 2027, and Summer 2027 semesters and may be considered if a vacancy becomes available within the academic year.If you have applied to previous pools in this discipline, you will need to apply to this pool to continue to be considered.WHAT YOU'LL DOUnder the general direction of a dean, an Instructor (Non-Contact/Temporary) provides comprehensive classroom instruction to students from diverse backgrounds for the purpose of facilitating the attainment of their academic or vocational objectives. In accordance with the provisions of Education Code sections 87482.5, Instructors (Non-Contract/Temporary) may be employed up to 67% of a full-time assignment. WHO WE AREThe Ventura County Community College District (VCCCD) is a public community college district serving residents throughout Ventura County. VCCCD's three colleges - Moorpark College, Oxnard College, and Ventura College - offer programs for transfer to four-year colleges and universities; career technical training, basic skills instruction; as well as community service, economic development, and continuing education for cultural growth, life enrichment, and skills improvement.The Ventura County Community College District recognizes that a diverse community of faculty, staff, and administrators promotes academic excellence and creates an inclusive educational and work environment for its employees, contractors, students, and the community it serves. With the understanding that a diverse community fosters multicultural awareness, promotes mutual understanding and respect, and provides role models for all students, VCCCD is committed to recruiting and employing a diverse and qualified group of administrators, faculty, and staff members who are dedicated to the success of all college students.The Ventura County Community College District does not engage in any employment practice that discriminates against any employee or applicant for employment on the basis of ethnic group identification, race, color, language, accent, immigration status, ancestry, national origin, political beliefs, age, gender, sex, religion, transgender, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, and/or physical or mental disability.Representative DutiesProvide academic instruction to students through lecture, lab, or performance courses; assess and develop cognitive abilities, communication skills, and higher order thinking skills among students through appropriate assignments and activities in one-on-one, classroom, and distance mediated instructional settings. EAdvise and instruct students regarding programs of study, other institutions of higher education, lifelong learning resources, and effective study skills; refer students to support services, programs, resources, and other professionals as appropriate. EObserve and evaluate student performance in meeting course objectives and student learning outcomes through assignments, projects, discussions, and examinations; provide feedback in a timely manner to student inquiries in class, online, or during established consultation office hours. EPlan and organize instruction according to approved course outlines and student learning outcomes to maximize student learning in alignment with department, college, and district goals; implement the student performance objectives as listed on the official course outline of record. EMaintain current, accurate records of course enrollment, attendance, student academic progress, course curriculum, and student learning outcomes; prepare and submit data and reports related to course and student progress in a timely manner. EEvaluate and select instructional materials such as textbooks, manuals, software, and tools in collaboration, as appropriate, with discipline faculty; order instructional materials according to campus bookstore procedure to ensure timely delivery. ERevise and update course content and materials of instruction in accordance with new theory, application, and industry developments within the discipline or area of specialization. EUpdate syllabi; collaborate with discipline faculty on a regular basis to assess and revise measurable student performance indicators for each course. EMay participate in curriculum and program development; may provide input into the development of student learning outcomes.May attend and participate on committees and in department, division, campus, and district meetings.May participate in articulation and matriculation related activities.May provide work direction to others.Perform related duties as assigned.E = Essential DutiesMinimum QualificationsCandidates must possess the minimum qualifications for the discipline as approved by the California Community Colleges Board of Governors and defined in the https://www.cccco.edu/-/media/CCCCO-Website/docs/report/19theditionminimumqualifications18a11y.pdf?la=en&hash=2B52FBA3909455ABF86B21533B5BB497A7742866Any bachelor's degree or higher and two years of professional experienceORAny associate degree and six years of professional experience.Professional experience is required when the applicant possesses a master's degree. The professional experience required must be directly related to the faculty member's teaching assignmentORthe equivalent*ORpossession of an appropriate California Community College Credential.Professional experience is required when the applicant possesses a master's degree.The professional experience required must be directly related to the faculty member's teaching assignment.All coursework must be from a recognized accredited college or university.If you have competed your education at an institution outside of the United States, please see the section below titled "Foreign Transcripts" for additional information.*EQUIVALENCYThe Ventura County Community College District, in its desire to select outstanding faculty members from the largest possible pool of qualified applicants, recognizes the fact that candidates may attain expertise in a discipline through a variety of means. Certain combinations of education, experience and other accomplishments in the field may be judged by the District as equal to the stated minimum qualifications for this position. Candidates whose transcripts do not list the title of their degree exactly as listed above, but feel they possess such equivalent qualifications are encouraged to complete and submit the https://www.vcccd.edu/sites/default/files/departments/human-resources/supplemental_questionnaire_for_equivalency_03.05.15_0.pdf https://get.adobe.com/reader/ with their application for review by the Districtwide Equivalency Committee.Example:Minimum Qualifications state: "Master's degree in agriculture".Candidate's transcripts state: "Master's degree in agricultural science".Since the degree on the candidate's transcripts in the example do not EXACTLY MATCH the degree listed in the minimum qualifications section, this candidate MUST complete the https://www.vcccd.edu/sites/default/files/departments/human-resources/supplemental_questionnaire_for_equivalency_03.05.15_0.pdf https://get.adobe.com/reader/ in order to be considered. When completing the form, be sure to explain in detail how your qualifications are equivalent to the required minimum qualifications. Do not assume that you do not need to submit a Supplemental Questionnaire for Equivalency because your degree is similar to a degree stated in the minimum qualifications. Degree titles that are not an exact match will not be considered outside of the equivalency process.The equivalency review is an independent process for district wide disciplines that is separate from the recruitment process to fill a vacancy. A subcommittee of discipline experts that is coordinated by an Academic Senate President will review the equivalency materials and make a recommendation as to whether or not the applicant demonstrated they have qualifications that are equivalent to those shown in the minimum qualifications section of the job posting. For disciplines that are unique to a specific campus the equivalency may be done by the hiring committee along with an Academic Senate President. Please be aware that the hiring committee may not be able to wait for the results from the equivalency review due to various time constraints and may need to move forward with the recruitment process.For further details regarding equivalency and the criteria by which equivalency may be granted, please review https://go.boarddocs.com/ca/vcccd/Board.nsf/goto?open&id=83LDBP0DD9E5 and https://go.boarddocs.com/ca/vcccd/Board.nsf/goto?open&id=88NT6K75D7D6.Supplemental InformationSELECTION PROCESSIf a vacancy in this discipline becomes available at one of the campuses, the applications in this pool will be reviewed by the hiring department. Only complete application packets that include the required documents and that meet the minimum qualifications (or that have been determined to possess equivalent qualifications) will be reviewed. The candidates deemed most qualified for the position will be invited to an interview. When completing the application and the supplemental questions, it is important to outline in detail your education, training (classes, seminars, workshops), and experience. You will be evaluated based upon the information provided.APPLICATION PROCEDUREIf you need assistance using the online application system please contact the GovernmentJobs.com applicant support line at (855) 524-5627 between the hours of 6 AM to 5 PM, Pacific Time, Monday through Friday.All applicants, including previous and current VCCCD employees, must submit the following documents with their application in order to be considered. All required documents must be submitted by the applicant. You may submit a new application once every 24 hours, but it must have all of the attachments as listed below. Failure to submit these materials may result in disqualification. Please note that only the most recent application submitted will be considered. 1. A completed Ventura County Community College District/GovernmentJobs.com Employment Application.All sections of the application must be filled out. Resumes are not a substitute for completing the "Work Experience" section of the employment application.2. Cover Letter.The cover letter of must include the following: A) the date, your name, and the position and locations for which you are applying, B) address your sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, social, economic, cultural, disability, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students, and C) provide the screening committee with an understanding of how you will contribute as a fully participating member of the VCCCD community.3. Resume4. Letters of recommendation (recommended, not required)If you choose to submit letters of recommendation, they should be uploaded with your application materials. We will not accept confidential letters of recommendation.5. Supplemental Questionnaire for Equivalency (if applicable)Please see the section titled "Equivalency" under the minimum qualifications above.6. Complete official or unofficial college/university transcriptsTranscripts must show the degree title and the date the degree was conferred, or the degree will not be considered for the purpose of determining if you meet minimum qualifications. Copies of diplomas will not be accepted in lieu of transcripts. If the qualifying degree has yet to be conferred and you expect to have the degree before you begin employment, you must submit transcripts that state the title of the degree you are working toward obtaining and indicate the anticipated completion date in your response to the associated supplemental question provided during the application process. An official copy of your transcripts will be required upon being hired. Instructors will not be allowed to start working until official transcripts have been received.FOREIGN TRANSCRIPTSIf you have completed coursework at a foreign institution that is not recognized as accredited by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) or the U.S. Department of Education, you must include a full evaluation of the foreign transcript with your application materials if you wish for us to consider the coursework. Visit the https://www.chea.org/state-licensed-or-authorized-institutions or the https://ope.ed.gov/dapip/#/home to search for institutions that are recognized as accredited. If you need your transcripts evaluated, please review the https://www.vcccd.edu/sites/default/files/media/pdf_document/2020/AGENCIES%20APPROVED%20FOR%20FOREIGN%20TRANSCRIPT%20EVALUATION.pdf https://get.adobe.com/reader/. If applicable, an official copy of your foreign transcript evaluation will also be required upon hire.PAY PHILOSOPHYStarting salaries for PT Faculty are based on educational achievement and relevant experience. Initial placement is within the starting salary range. Further advancements are based on longevity and educational growth. Please review the https://www.vcccd.edu/sites/default/files/media/pdf_document/2021/part-time_faculty_salary_explanation_fy21_02.24.21.pdf https://get.adobe.com/reader/ for more information.STARTING SALARYPart-time faculty with classroom assignments are paid between $2,007 and $3,108 per semester per 10% load.Part-time faculty salaries are governed by the collective bargaining agreement between the Ventura County Federation of College Teachers, AFT, Local 1828, AFL-CIO and the Ventura County Community College District. More information can be found in the https://www.vcccd.edu/sites/default/files/media/pdf_document/2023/2022-2025%20AFT%20-%20VCCCD%20Contract.pdf https://get.adobe.com/reader/.Please be aware that we will require verification of all part-time teaching experience for which you wish to receive credit toward placement on the salary schedule. You will have 30 days to provide verification upon receipt of the offer of employment. Verification must come from the human resources department and state the percentage of full-time-equivalent assignment you worked during the specified time period.Part-time faculty salaries are governed by the collective bargaining agreement between the Ventura County Federation of College Teachers, AFT, Local 1828, AFL-CIO and the Ventura County Community College District. You will have 30 days to provide verification upon receipt of the offer of employment. Verification must come from the human resources department and state the percentage of full-time-equivalent assignment you worked during the specified time period.ACCOMMODATIONSIndividuals who are invited to participate in the interview process who require a reasonable accommodation due to a disability, must notify the Ventura County Community College District Human Resources Department in writing at least two business days prior to the interview. The Director provides leadership in the implementation, configuration, integration, and lifecycle management of these systems, ensuring they effectively support instructional, student services, and administrative operations while meeting reporting and compliance requirements.Distinguishing Characteristics:The Director of Enterprise Applications serves as the District's primary technical resource for ERP-related systems and provides leadership and expertise in the configuration, integration, support, and data management processes associated with these applications. Working collaboratively with District and college stakeholders, the Director facilitates the effective use of ERP-related technologies to support student success and institutional operations and coordinates related technology initiatives and projects.Examples of Duties/Essential Functions:Duties/essential functions may include, but are not limited to, the following:• Plans, organizes, and directs the implementation, configuration, integration, and support of enterprise administrative systems, including ERP systems and related enterprise applications.• Oversees the lifecycle management of enterprise applications, including planning, upgrades, enhancements, and system replacements.• Collaborates with District and college departments to assess business needs and translate operational requirements into effective technology solutions.• Facilitates communication between technical staff and functional users to ensure systems support institutional processes and priorities.• Oversees the development and maintenance of system integrations between the ERP and other enterprise systems, including cloud-based and third-party applications.• Supervises and provides direction for staff responsible for enterprise applications, systems integration, application development, database administration, and related support functions.• Supports the District's data architecture by ensuring consistent, reliable, and secure access to institutional data across systems.• Ensures effective data exchange and integration through application programming interfaces (APIs), data interfaces, and other integration technologies.• Communicates complex technology issues clearly to non-technical parties, both orally and in writing, makes effective presentations, and ensures open communication between users and technical groups.• Coordinates user training and support activities.• Participates in long-range planning efforts and in the evaluation, costing, selection, testing, and implementation of all applications-related security, software, and hardware.• Ensures compliance with federal, state, and institutional requirements related to data privacy, security, and reporting, including efforts to optimize systems.• Reviews and is responsible for the documentation of systems.• Participates in the development and implementation of departmental procedures and operational standards, ensuring compliance, execution, and clear communication.• Participates in institutional risk management and technology continuity planning, with a focus on information security, system resilience, data protection, and the long-term sustainability and reliability of technology systems.• Develops and schedules priorities, assigns responsibilities, ensures efficient and timely completion of projects, and prepares time and cost estimates and progress reports.• Ensures the accurate and timely submission of Management Information Systems (MIS) data to the State Chancellor's Office.• Evaluates emerging technologies and enterprise software solutions to improve institutional effectiveness and operational efficiency.• Identifies opportunities to streamline institutional processes through technology solutions.• Confers with hardware and software vendors to obtain information, resolve problems, and arrange and conduct demonstrations and evaluations.• Collaborates with institutional research and data teams to ensure enterprise systems support institutional reporting and analytics.• Provides coaching, evaluation, and professional development opportunities for assigned staff.• Manages the Process Expert Teams (PET) annual budget.• Performs other duties as assigned.Minimum Qualifications:Education/Experience:EQUIVALENT COMBINATION OF TRAINING AND EXPERIENCE:Education/Training: Bachelor's degree from an accredited college with major coursework in computer science, management information systems, business, or related field. project management and change management methodologies; data governance, reporting systems, and regulatory reporting requirements applicable to higher education or similar environment; application security, access controls, and data privacy requirements; documentation, training, and support practices for enterprise systems.Skill To:N/AAbility To:Analyze complex operational and technical problems and develop effective, practical technology solutions; assess business requirements and translate them into functional and technical system solutions; plan, organize, and oversee the implementation, configuration, and ongoing support of enterprise applications; manage and prioritize multiple technology initiatives and projects; oversee the integration of enterprise systems and ensure reliable and secure data exchange across applications; ensure the integrity, security, and availability of enterprise data and systems; communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences both orally and in writing; develop and maintain collaborative working relationships with administrators, faculty, staff, and external vendors; plan, organize, assign, and evaluate the work of technical staff; facilitate cross-functional collaboration and support effective technology governance processes; and adapt to evolving technologies and institutional priorities while maintaining stable and reliable enterprise systems.Desirable Qualifications:- Significant experience administering, supporting, or enhancing student information systems, preferably Ellucian Colleague, and third-party integrations in a complex higher education environment.- Ability to communicate complex technical information clearly to executive leaders, functional departments, and end users.- Success building partnerships between technology teams and functional departments across multiple sites to establish shared priorities and develop organization-wide solutions.- Experience managing a portfolio of complex technology projects, aligning priorities, resources, and timelines with organizational goals.- Experience leading organizational change, promoting user adoption, and improving business processes to enhance efficiency and service delivery.- Success developing effective technology teams through coaching, professional development, collaboration, and accountability. jobs.title: Head of Schools and DIscipleship Ministry at Oceana Christian School
jobs.description: Employer: Oceana Christian School Expires: 11/27/2026 OverviewThe mission of Hart First Baptist Church is to make disciples of Jesus. We want to help people find real life inJesus Christ through real relationships with His Word and His people, the local church.Oceana Christian School (OCS) is a major ministry of First Baptist Church, serving preschool through 5th gradeand ministering to both FBC families and community families seeking a quality Christian education. We desireOCS to be a place where Christian education supports the shared discipleship work of the church and home,while also building meaningful relationships with families in our community.The Head of Schools & Discipleship Ministry is first and foremost the educational leader and Administrator ofOceana Christian School. This person will provide hands-on leadership to the school, support and developfaculty and staff, maintain strong academic standards, and foster a distinctly Christian educational environment.Working closely with teachers, staff, families, church leadership, and designated support personnel, the Head ofSchools will guide the school's day-to-day operations and help evaluate its long-term health, direction, andsustainability.The initial focus of this role will be almost exclusively on Oceana Christian School. We recognize thateffective leadership begins with listening, learning, and building relationships. The person stepping into thisposition will need time to become acquainted with the school, understand its culture and operations, establishtrust with faculty and staff, and identify opportunities to support and strengthen the school's ministry. We wantthis person to have the time and freedom to learn the school well before taking on significant additionalresponsibilities.Over time, we desire for this person to take on a growing role in FBC's broader discipleship ministry. The scopeand nature of those responsibilities will develop in keeping with the person's gifting, abilities, and interests, aswell as the needs of the church. Our goal is not to add a second full-time ministry to an already demandingschool leadership role, but to build on the strengths of the individual God brings to our church andschool community.We believe the work of ministry belongs to the whole church. Our leaders are called to equip God's people to doHis work, empowering FBC members to participate actively in worship, teaching, discipleship, service, andcommunicating the gospel to the world. We desire a Head of Schools who embraces this vision andunderstands the unique opportunity to connect Christian education, family discipleship, and the life of the localchurch.Qualifications● Demonstrates a mature Christian faith, a servant heart, and clear dependence on the Lord in leadership.● Agrees with and supports Hart FBC's Statement of Faith.● Loves the local church and understands and values the relationship between FBC and Oceana ChristianSchool.● Has a genuine passion for Christian education, learning, and academic excellence.● Holds a high standard for education while thoughtfully developing an approach that reflects the mission anddistinctives of Christian education.● Holds a degree or advanced degree in education, educational leadership, biblical studies, leadership, or arelated field, or possesses equivalent experience.● Preferred degrees include a bachelor's or advanced degree in education, an MA in Christian Education orLeadership, an MDiv, or a four-year degree in a related field.● Experience in Christian education, school administration, educational leadership, ministry, or a comparableleadership setting preferred.● Meets the biblical qualifications for a ministry leader as described in 1 Timothy 3 and Titus 1.● Understands and supports FBC's practice of male eldership. If a male candidate is selected, we would likehim to consider applying as Pastor of Education and Discipleship.Core Competencies● Christian & Servant Leadership: Leads with humility, care, and a willingness to serve people at every levelof the school and church ministries.● Educational Leadership: Loves learning, values strong teaching, and is committed to maintaining highacademic standards within a distinctly Christian educational philosophy.● Relational Leadership: Builds trust with church members, teachers, staff, parents, students, andcommunity families.● Listening & Staff Support: Values the perspective of teachers and staff, listens well to those closest to theday-to-day work, and looks for practical ways to help them succeed.● Communication: Communicates clearly, consistently, and proactively.● Follow-Through: Is dependable, takes ownership of responsibilities, and does what he says he will do.● Administration & Financial Stewardship: Possesses strong organizational skills and is comfortableworking with budgets, financial information, and basic bookkeeping oversight.● Facilitation & Equipping: Looks for ways to remove obstacles, meet practical needs, and equip others tocarry out their responsibilities effectively.● Teamwork: Works collaboratively with school staff, church staff, support personnel, and the other elders.Areas of Responsibility1. Oceana Christian School Administration & LeadershipThe primary responsibility of the Head of Schools & Discipleship Ministry is serving as the Administrator ofOceana Christian School. This person will provide spiritual, educational, and administrative leadership to OCS,working closely with faculty, staff, families, church leadership, and designated support staff.During the initial season of service, the primary emphasis will be on becoming acquainted with the school,understanding its current practices and needs, building relationships, and providing consistent support to facultyand staff. As this foundation is established, the Head of Schools will lead ongoing efforts to strengthen theschool's programs, culture, and long-term sustainability.● Provide day-to-day leadership and oversight of school operations in cooperation with support staff● Serve as the spiritual leader of OCS faculty and staff● Maintain and strengthen a distinctly Christian culture throughout the school● Listen to teachers and staff, value their on-the-ground perspective, and look for practical ways to help themsucceed● Oversee curriculum review and selection, including biblical integration● Maintain strong academic standards and promote a culture of learning and educational excellence● Conduct regular staff observations and annual evaluations● Recruit, hire, develop, and when necessary terminate OCS staff● Communicate clearly and consistently with faculty, staff, parents, and church leadership● Serve as the primary administrative point of contact for faculty, staff, and families● Serve as the public face of OCS to the church and wider community● Recruit new students and support enrollment growth● Build relationships with OCS families, including community families who may have little or no currentconnection to FBC● Help create pathways for OCS families to become connected to the life and ministry of FBC● Develop and manage the annual school budget and provide appropriate financial oversight● Schedule and oversee professional development for faculty and staff● Manage the shared-time agreement with North Muskegon Public Schools● Work with church leadership to evaluate the long-term health, direction, and sustainability of OCS2. Discipleship LeadershipOur desire is to develop a robust culture of discipleship at FBC through a clear and intentional ministry modelthat strengthens both church-based discipleship and discipleship within the home.The Head of Schools & Discipleship Ministry will, over time, take on some responsibilities that contribute to thebroader discipleship ministry of FBC. The nature and scope of this involvement will be shaped by the individual'sgifting and abilities, the needs of the church, and the foundation established through service at OCS.We believe effective ministry leadership means equipping others rather than personally leading every ministry.As this aspect of the role develops, the Head of Schools will work alongside the elders and ministry leaders toidentify opportunities for greater alignment, strengthen existing ministries, and help equip people to grow in theirfaith and become disciple-makers themselves.Potential areas of involvement:Depending on the strengths of the candidate, they could...● Help assess FBC's current discipleship ministries, structures, and pathways.● Contribute to the development and implementation of a clear church-wide discipleship model.● Identify gaps, overlap, and opportunities for greater alignment between ministries.● Recruit, equip, coach, and develop ministry leaders and volunteers.● Provide vision, resources, and support to ministries that fall under the broader discipleship umbrella,including:● Small groups, Bible studies, home groups, and mentoring ministries● Adult and children's Sunday School● Wednesday children's ministries● Men's and women's ministries● Family and home discipleship● Help establish clear pathways for people to connect, grow, serve, and become disciple-makers.● Participate in the teaching, shepherding, and broader ministry of FBC according to gifting and need.These responsibilities are intended to develop gradually, not to compete with the initial priority ofleading Oceana Christian School well. The candidate would not be expected to participate in all activitiesmentioned above.Responsible ToThe Head of Schools & Discipleship Ministry serves within the leadership structure of Hart First Baptist Churchand is accountable to the elders and the congregation.

jobs.title: Western PA Long-term, Building Subs and Day-to-day Substitute Teachers at Precision HR Solutions
jobs.description: Employer: Precision HR Solutions Expires: 11/27/2026 Precision HR Solutions is partnered with many school districts in western Pennsylvania and looking for "Building Substitute Teachers," "Day-to-day Substitute Teachers" and several “Long-term Substitute Teachers” to assist with continuity of instruction for the 2026 - 2027 school year. For the recent teacher graduates and those currently completing their student teaching assignments graduating in the coming months, these are great opportunities providing you with valuable, practical experience to build your resumes as you journey through the first steps of your new career! If you haven't secured the opportunity you were looking for or you're a student teacher getting close to graduation and your first teaching job, we have plenty of options for you to consider until you secure the full-time or contract opportunity you are looking for. For the experienced teacher looking for a change or between assignments, we're here to help keep you working and bridge the gap (even if only temporarily) until you accept your next assignment. jobs.title: NACA Housing Counselor at Neighborhood Assistance Corporation of America
jobs.description: Employer: Neighborhood Assistance Corporation of America Expires: 11/27/2026 NACA HOUSING COUNSELORNACA Offices NationwideCOMPENSATION: $65,000 to $100,000+ (including substantial production incentives) FLSA: Non-Exempt LOCATION: NACA Offices Nationwide CONTACT: jobs@naca.com BENEFITS: Comprehensive package: single/family health, vision, dental, 401(k) and more WEBSITE: www.naca.com NACA HOUSING COUNSELOR: The NACA Housing Counselor serves as the primary point of contact from the initial counseling session through closing (referred herein as “NACA Counselor”). The Housing Counselor assists low-and-moderate income people, and those subjected to systemic racism to achieve affordable homeownership (referred herein as “Members”) with the best mortgage in America while earning considerable income. NACA’s Best in America Mortgage outstanding terms are – no down payment, no closing cost, no mortgage insurance, no credit score consideration, at a below market fixed interest rate. The NACA mortgage and its homeownership programs are superior to other homeownership programs. NACA Housing Counselors are provided an instant pipeline of homebuyers. The NACA Housing Counselor’s performance requirements and compensation is performance based with pay incentivizing positive outcomes for the Members they work with. NACA Housing Counselors continued employment is contingent on successful completion of their NACA training, becoming HUD-Certified, and licensed as a Mortgage Loan Originator (“MLO”) in the state/s where her/his office originates NACA loans. JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:The NACA House Counselor manages a pipeline of Member files assigned to her/him and provides comprehensive, individual housing and financial management counseling services in a local NACA office with in-person or video counseling. The Housing Counselor provides comprehensive housing and financial management. S/he assesses the Members’ readiness for homeownership and determines an affordable mortgage payment considering each Member’s particular circumstances and goals based on NACA’s policies and procedures. This includes helping Members overcome the roadblocks preventing them from qualifying for a mortgage loan and purchasing a home including obtaining necessary information and documents. The NACA Housing Counselor ensures effective and timely communication including explaining the mortgage qualification criteria. The NACA Housing Counselor also works with Members to address and improve their financial management skills. In addition, NACA Housing Counselors must be knowledgeable with all of NACA programs to provide counseling, assistance and solutions to homebuyers, homeowners, and renters with an unaffordable housing payment. The NACA Housing Counselor utilizes NACA’s state-of-the-art client management system software called NACA-Lynx and the NACA Portal which enables paperless comprehensive housing counseling and mortgage processing. The NACA Housing Counselor works with Members to become qualified for the NACA Mortgage based on NACA’s character-based underwriting criteria and compensating factors (“NACA Qualification”). The NACA Qualification is also appropriate for qualifying for other mortgages, and the NACA Counselor should provide Members with three mortgage options. While NACA Qualification can be achieved quickly for some Members, it may take several months or longer for others. A NACA Underwriter reviews the NACA Counselor’s assessment to confirm if the Member should be NACA Qualified or requires additional counseling or documentation. NACA Housing Counselors are provided with support staff and processes to assist in their success. The NACA Housing Counselor utilizes problem solving skills and financial management guidance to help Members achieve affordable homeownership always maintaining a professional appearance and demeanor while providing outstanding customer services. She/he must be able to work independently with Members and in coordination with other NACA departments. The NACA Housing Counselor must manage their time effectively to provide accurate, comprehensive counseling sessions within specified time limits. The NACA Housing Counselor provides comprehensive housing counseling as well as the mortgage related activities described below. The NACA Housing Counselor’s daily responsibilities include working with Members on the following: Provide a clear direction for a path towards their homeownership goals and improve their financial management skills. Utilize NACA-Lynx and NACA Portal to accurately complete documentation and data entry for efficient and paperless NACA Qualification and mortgage processing. Document files with written narratives and identify action items for the Members to complete after each counseling session. Review payment history, income, liabilities, assets, and other criteria to determine eligibility for the program, readiness for home ownership and mortgage payment affordability. Review and address Members’ savings pattern including a reduction in the Members’ expenses. This includes calculating a monthly cash flow surplus to establish a Member’s long term affordable mortgage payment. Work with Members for as long as it takes to resolve payment history issues, to reduce debt and/or adjust expenses as needed to meet their purchase goals. Define a plan to save the required Purchase Funds necessary for the home purchase. Determine a maximum affordable mortgage payment and define a path to achieve Member’s homeownership purchase price/goal. Examine and process documents and address document issues as needed. Address NACA Qualification conditions (if any) within 48 hours. Provide information on three mortgage products and options for the Member to make a well-informed home purchase and mortgage decision. Assist Members to purchase within their affordability and eligibility.Maintain communication during the Member’s housing search to address any changes to the criteria used for their NACA Qualification Process and provide a Property Specific Letter for Members during their housing search. Review and process Member’s application for NACA Credit Access to ensure the Member and the property adhere to NACA’s criteria. Assist in submitting the Member’s mortgage application. Address lender conditions. Assist the Member through closing to facilitate the mortgage process. Other Activities and Requirements:Present Home Buyer Workshops. Assist in outreach activities focused on low- and moderate-income communities, churches, job sites, events, etc. Participate in regular trainings.Participate in NACA events and campaigns. Other duties as assigned. Advocacy in Support of NACA’s Mission Participate in advocacy campaigns as needed. NACA continues its aggressive advocacy in fighting for economic justice for low to moderate income and people of color by addressing the racial wealth disparity gap and other issues. Employment with NACA requires ongoing participation in NACA’s advocacy, campaigns, outreach, community organizing, and other activities as determined by NACA. This includes supporting and actively promoting NACA’s tactics and mission of fighting for economic justice. This is also important for NACA’s continued success and in expanding NACA’s purchase and other programs. NACA staff have a tremendous impact on the Members and communities they serve. For more information about NACA or its history and programs, visit www.naca.com. COMPENSATION: NACA Housing Counselor’s total compensation consists of Base Pay, Overtime, Performance Pay, and Monthly Bonus Payment (must be a licensed MLO to receive Performance Pay and a Monthly Bonus). NACA does not allow any NACA employee to charge the Members or others for any service provided, nor to add any product to the loan, receive a referral fee, or do anything else to increase compensation. NACA Housing Counselor’s compensation is structured to allow her/him to earn an overall compensation from $60,000 to $100,000+ with a significant portion from Performance Pay. Performance Payment is significantly higher for services provided to Members in greatest need of NACA’s program(s). These Members are low to moderate income Members and higher income Members purchasing in low to moderate income areas (“Priority Members”). NACA’s purchase program is so outstanding that a significant portion of the compensation is the Performance Pay for the below outcomes subject to criteria and counseling requirements. The NACA Counselor should make the following with the opportunity and expectation to earn more. The Base Pay is to compensate for outreach, NACA’s advocacy campaigns, and other activities set forth by NACA and not to be considered the main source of compensation. NACA Housing Counselors may be required to participate in NACA campaigns and events, which may occur on weekends, weekdays, or require extended hours. The compensation for these events may be different than what is stated herein as determined at NACA’s sole discretion. Base Pay: $15.00 per hour, or greater if required by state law, plus any applicable overtime. $42,000 annually. NACA Qualification Payment: $100 per NACA Qualification $12,000 annually (10 NACA Qualifications per month meeting requirements) NACA Closings: $850 per Priority Member plus overtime pay – $900 per Priority Member Total Compensation: $86,400 annually The Base Pay is to compensate for outreach, NACA’s advocacy campaigns, and other activities set forth by NACA and not to be considered the main source of compensation. NACA Counselors may be required to participate in NACA campaigns and events, which may occur on weekends, weekdays, or require extended hours. The compensation for these events may be different than what is stated herein as determined at NACA’s sole discretion. TIME DEMANDS: A NACA Housing Counselor works approximately 45 to 50+ hours weekly and as necessary to meet the demands of the job. Basic work hours are: 8:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. weekdays and some late night(s). Two Saturdays are additionally required every month for homebuyer workshops and/or counseling scheduled from 8:30 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. A NACA Housing Counselor may be required to work increased hours and weekends for campaigns, events, and other activities at NACA’s sole discretion. NACA Housing Counselors must maintain punctuality to ensure accountability to team members, management, and their assigned Members. NACA Housing Counselors are required to work from a NACA office where they can be most effective and receive ongoing support.TRAINING & DEVELOPMENT: NACA Housing Counselors must demonstrate effective counseling, understanding of NACA’s policies and procedures, and obtain their licenses and certifications during the 10-week training and development period, which NACA may change at its discretion (“Development Period”). During the Development Period the NACA Housing Counselors must: 1. HUD Certified through the HUD certification process; 2. Licensed MLO through the National Mortgage Licensing System; and 3. Registration and Enrollment Support • Assist with registration outreach campaigns. • Contact students who have not registered and assist in removing barriers to enrollment. Front Desk Operations • Serve as a welcoming first point of contact for students visiting the Advising and Accessibility offices. • Provide front desk coverage and support for the third-floor student services area. • Greet students and visitors and provide wayfinding assistance. • Answer questions regarding services, appointments, campus resources, and university processes. Testing Center Operations • Assist in daily operation of the Testing Center. • Schedule and coordinate testing appointments for students with disabilities. • Monitor testing sessions and ensure compliance with testing procedures. • Support accommodation-related testing processes in collaboration with Accessibility Services staff. Skills Required: • Strong interpersonal and communication skills to engage all students, faculty and staff, employers, and other visitors professionally and respectfully. • Organizational skills with attention to detail for accurate data entry, document preparation, and file management. • Proficiency and/or willingness to learn Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and familiarity with tools like Canva or Microsoft Teams for creating and managing content. • Commitment to maintaining confidentiality with student records under FERPA guidelines and sensitive career information. • Ability to take initiative, prioritize tasks, and work independently or collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. • A proactive and service-oriented mindset, with a commitment to supporting student success. • Adaptability and eagerness to learn new skills through training and hands-on experience

Lead and engage community volunteers in projects in coordination with project liaisons and MCC staff. Crew Member Mentorship: Serve as educators, mentors, and positive role models for team members.Foster a supportive, inclusive, and professional learning environment.Encourage personal growth, accountability, teamwork, and leadership development while helping members build confidence, independence, and a strong service ethic.Train and coach members in all aspects of trail construction, maintenance, and rehabilitation, including proper tools use, trail building techniques, erosion control, site restoration, and the application of conservation best practices.Provide constructive feedback and adapt instruction to meet varying experience levels.Guide and support team members throughout project activities, prioritizing their physical safety, overall wellbeing, and team success.Participate in and facilitate professional development activities that prepare members for future employment, education, and career opportunities.Support the development of transferrable skills, including communication, problem solving, conflict resolution, time management, teamwork, leadership, and professionalism.Essential Functions:Have the desire to learn, serve others, and make a positive difference in communities and the environment.Ability to serve as a positive role model and uphold MCC’s values, policies, and expectations.Willingness and physical ability to serve on a variety of conservation projects, including the use of power and hand tools.Ability to perform heavy lifting, bending, and carrying up to 50 pounds on trails with steep, uneven and rugged terrain.Ability and willingness to serve in extremes of heat and cold and exposure to wildlife, including biting and stinging insects.High level of comfort outdoors and willingness to serve, live, eat, and camp in all weather conditions and remote locations.Ability to hike 2-8 miles per day in rugged terrain, often carrying gear and tools.Ability to perform tasks as part of a cooperative team.Responsible, dependable, adaptable, and capable of exercising sound judgement.Excellent organizational and communication skills.Interest in personal growth and in participating in ongoing training.Ability to build respectful, inclusive, and productive relationships with individuals from a variety of backgrounds and experiences.Willingness and ability to uphold MCC health, safety, and risk management protocols and to support members in maintaining a safe service environment.Marginal Functions:The ability to operate an MCC vehicle to transport members and gear to and from project sitesThis position does not have recurring access to vulnerable populations.What to Expect: This is an opportunity to live and serve in some of Maine’s most remote and beautiful places while taking on meaningful conservation initiatives. jobs.title: Crisis Support Specialist, Part Time at Thresholds
jobs.description: Employer: Thresholds Expires: 11/27/2026 When people experience in McHenry County experience a mental health crisis, they are faced with the decision to go to the emergency department or to try to manage the crisis themselves. The Living Room McHenry offers an alternative: a community crisis center—a welcoming, accepting, and calm environment where Crisis Support Specialists provide advocacy, information, and peer support. As a Crisis Support Specialist, you will use your personal experience with mental health recovery to support and educate Living Room guests on managing crisis. You will engage guests in conversation to hear their stories, learn about their interests and strengths, and respectfully encourage them to take steps in their recovery process. Over the course of the day, you may model coping strategies, help guests develop their own crisis recovery plans, and/or link guests with supportive services for after their crisis. A welcoming environment is key to the success of the Living Room, so you will greet guests and learn their names as part of inviting them to take the lead in determining their recovery path. Crisis Support Specialists will also prepare food for guests and ensure that the space is neat and tidy. Keep up to date on current trends in the mental health field and deepen your knowledge of evidence-based practices through ample training opportunities to enhance Living Room services. You can also gain supervision for CRSS certification and reimbursement for testing and application fees. To succeed in this role, you need: Lived experience of mental health recovery preferred but not requiredEffective communication and relationship-building Good writing skills Strong time management and organization To be at least 21 years old Many education and experience paths are eligible for this role: High school diploma or GED certificate required Higher education in Psychology, Social Work, Counseling or related field preferred Certified Recovery Support Specialist (CRSS) preferred Part Time Shifts Available:Friday 3:00pm - 11:30pmSaturday: 7:00am - 3:30pmSaturday: 3:00pm - 11:30pmSaturday: 11:00pm - 7:30amSunday: 7:00am - 3:30pmSunday: 11:00pm - 7:30amWhat sets Thresholds apart: Competitive pay - Base Rate: $25.50- $29.13 per hourBased on education, experience, and licensureGenerous PTO403(b) retirement plan with 3% employer match Robust employee assistance program (EAP)Public service loan forgiveness Thresholds is a mission-driven agency with a deep commitment to fostering an environment where all feel valued and respected, a place where every employee can be themselves, thrive, and support the agency’s mission. jobs.title: Security Counselor at Minnesota Direct Care and Treatment
jobs.description: Employer: Minnesota Direct Care and Treatment - MSOP Expires: 11/27/2026 Applicants may be eligible for a hiring bonus of up to $2,500!Starting wage $26.86 with shift differentials available! Full-Time and Part-Time positions available!This is an opportunity to be part of an organization that is committed to our staff, clients, and the community. The Minnesota Sex Offender Program serves people who are court ordered to receive sex offender treatment via the civil commitment process. Program staff provide comprehensive services including therapy, education programming, therapeutic recreation, vocational programming and volunteer services, health and wellness to clients in a therapeutic environment where safety and security are at the forefront of all campus activities.Security Counselors provide supervision to clients who are civilly committed to the Minnesota Sex Offender Program (MSOP). In this role, the Security Counselor utilizes a team approach to ensure a safe, secure and therapeutic environment in which the clients work towards successful community reintegration. Working in this environment may present a variety of unique and unforeseen situations which require the Security Counselor to respond in a calm manner that de-escalates and prevents potentially dangerous situations. Job duties and responsibilities for the Security Counselor position includes:To ensure safety, security, and control is maintained within the facility through consistent and systematic application of established policies/procedures.To provide and ensure consistent, fair and humane treatment of clients during the course of daily activities.To provide and receive information in an accurate, timely and dependable manner.To be competent in the use of security, electrical, mechanical, electronic, and all other equipment associated with the position.To be prepared for and respond to any unusual or emergency situations.To act in a professional manner and set a good example both on and off the job.To use time wisely and to the benefit of the facility.To be knowledgeable of and support facility post orders, operating guidelines, instructions, security procedures, and division directives that apply to the duties assigned and to enhance operational methods.Note: This announcement will be used to fill multiple permanent, full-time, part-time, and/or intermittent (on-call), Security Counselor vacancies within the Minnesota Sex Offender Program (MSOP) in Moose Lake. The shifts may be day, evening, or overnight. Why Work For MSOPYou owe it to yourself to check out this exciting and rewarding career at MSOP with Direct Care and Treatment, the behavioral health care system operated by the Department of Human Services.Led by seasoned and respected professionals, MSOP is a comprehensive sex offense specific treatment program in a modified therapeutic community in a secure setting. MSOP is committed to the professional growth of staff and applying current best practices to assist our clients in making meaningful change. MSOP, while rooted in public safety, is focused on the capacity to clients to change and ultimately be reintegrated into the community when risk to the public is sufficiently reduced. Working for the Minnesota Department of Human Services Direct Care & Treatment division PAYS!In addition to a rewarding career in which you will be positively impacting the lives of Minnesota’s most vulnerable residents, we provide competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package. This includes a competitive hourly wage, affordable insurance, retirement benefits, paid time off and more!When you start a career with us, you may also be eligible for:Up to $2,500 Hiring Bonus*Annual pay increasesCorrections Early Retirement Program Minimum QualificationsTo qualify applicants must have:A High School diploma or GED and be at least 18 years of age and least ONE of the following in order to qualify for further consideration:One or more years of full-time work experience in ANY field; ORTwo or more years of part-time work experience in ANY field.Preferred QualificationsOne (1) year of volunteer/work experience which demonstrates skills in human relations capacity sufficient to assist in the resolution of disputes; provide ongoing support and direction to clients and facilitate living, social, and leisure activities.Ability to implement treatment strategies, and recognize and report sudden behavioral and physical changes to appropriate staff OR training in therapeutic intervention and behavior management.Our employees are dedicated to ensuring cultural responsiveness. Preferred candidates will have a variety of experiences working effectively with others from different backgrounds and cultures.Apply online at https://mn.gov/mmb/careers/ to Job ID 87545

Carlos clinic, with occasional opportunities for virtual parent intakes, parent consultation, or other support when clinically appropriate.We offer meaningful scheduling flexibility and will work collaboratively to develop a schedule that supports your desired caseload and professional goals while meeting the needs of the clinic and the families we serve.We also provide dedicated clinical and administrative support with scheduling, intake and records coordination, billing and practice systems, communication and coordination, documentation support, clinical resources, technology, and other day-to-day practice needs.Compensation & Benefits$80–$95 per 50-minute clinical session, based on relevant experience, expertise, specialized training, and responsibilities.Approved nonclinical responsibilities, including documentation, multidisciplinary team meetings, clinical consultation, required or approved training, and other approved practice responsibilities, are separately compensated.This is a W-2 employee position.Depending on employment status, role, eligibility, and applicable plan terms, NDC benefits and professional supports may include:• Employer-subsidized health insurance for eligible full-time employees, including support for dependent child coverage • 401(k) retirement benefits with an employer contribution/match for eligible employees • Paid time off • Professional liability insurance for eligible clinical services provided through NDC • Professional-development and specialized-training support based on role and eligibility • Wellness benefits for eligible employees • Collective Kids Grant, providing eligible full-time employees with support toward qualifying child-related expenses such as childcare, camps, tutoring, educational resources, and enrichment activities • Paid required and approved training, as applicableWho We Hope to FindWe are looking for a clinician who:• Holds a current, active California license as a Psychologist, perspective • Understands children within the context of development, regulation, relationships, communication, environment, strengths, and individual differences • Can thoughtfully adapt therapy to different developmental, cognitive, communication, and regulatory profiles • Values children’s autonomy, dignity, strengths, and authentic identities • Enjoys collaborating with families and other professionals • Values interdisciplinary thinking and teamwork • Is thoughtful, reliable, and able to work independently while contributing to a collaborative team • Is committed to continued learning and professional growth • Is interested in beginning part-time with the opportunity to grow toward full-timeInterested?
